title: Unifying Charge-Learnability Transitions in U(1)-Symmetric Quantum Circuits through Informational Power of Local Measurement
abstract: Charge-learnability transitions in monitored symmetric quantum circuits reveal how local measurement records acquire sufficient information to infer a conserved charge. Here we extend charge learnability to probabilistic weak measurements, for which the measurement probability and measurement strength are independently tunable. We find that the learnability phase boundary is organized by the informational power of local measurement. We further introduce cross entropy as a label-sensitive diagnostic that distinguishes unbiased, biased, and antibiased decoder variants. Finally, the exact record--label mutual information provides a decoder-independent benchmark for the information fundamentally available for charge inference. Our results establish informational power of local measurement as a unifying principle for charge learnability under general monitoring protocols.
summary: This paper analyzes how reliably one can infer a conserved charge in a quantum circuit by monitoring it using weak measurements. The authors demonstrate that the transition point where inference becomes possible is fundamentally governed by the local informational power extracted during the measurement process. This establishes a unified theoretical principle linking different types of quantum monitoring protocols.
main_problem: The research extends the study of charge learnability transitions from standard projective measurements to probabilistic weak measurements in quantum circuits.
main_result: The learnability phase boundary is shown to be organized by the local informational power of the measurement, providing a unifying principle across different monitoring protocols.
method: The authors use Bayesian decoding techniques and calculate various information-theoretic measures, including cross entropy and record–label mutual information, to diagnose charge inference capability.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional U(1)-symmetric quantum circuit (chain of L qubits) evolving under random charge-conserving two-qubit gates. Monitoring involves probabilistic weak measurements controlled by probability (q) and strength (eta).
key_observables: Charge learnability, Cross Entropy, Record–Label Mutual Information, Binder Ratio.
important_parameters: Measurement probability ($q$) and measurement strength ($\eta$); the local informational power $I_{	ext{loc}}(q, \eta)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares different decoder variants (unbiased, biased, antibiased) to isolate the fundamental information limit from decoding efficiency.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing how transition boundaries are organized by constant values of local informational power ($I_{	ext{loc}}$), comparing results across various decoders and measurement regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the weak measurement protocol, then introducing multiple diagnostic tools (cross-entropy, mutual information) to characterize learnability, ultimately establishing the role of local informational power as the unifying organizing principle for the transition boundary.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous framework connecting fundamental concepts from quantum information theory (mutual information) with physical observables in open quantum systems (measurement records), which is highly relevant for understanding measurement-induced dynamics and control.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of charge learnability in a monitored U(1)-symmetric quantum circuit and its phase diagram in terms of the measurement probability q and measurement strength η. (a) The circuit is initialized in one of two neigh- boring charge sectors. Random charge-conserving two-qubit gates are arranged in alternating even- and odd-bond lay- ers, each followed by a probabilistic local weak-measurement layer. The resulting spacetime record is processed by a de- coder to infer the hidden charge label. (b) A transition bound- ary separates the failure and success regimes and is organized by the measurement informational power.

FIG. 2. Finite-size diagnostics for the unbiased decoder at measurement probability q = 1, with measurement strength η varied along the horizontal axis. The representative condition Iloc ≃0.20 predicts η0 ≃0.277. (a) Decoding accuracy. (b) Binder ratio of the binary posterior entropy. (c) Cross-entropy variance Var(C). The vertical dashed line marks the selected Binder crossing or variance peak.

FIG. 4. Decoder-independent and decoder-dependent charge-learnability boundaries in the plane of measurement probability q and measurement strength η. The red solid curve denotes the decoder-independent finite-size boundary inferred from the exact record–label mutual information, Iloc ≃0.16. The three blue curves denote the biased, un- biased, and antibiased transition estimates, with Iloc ≃0.17, 0.20, and 0.25, respectively. Open markers indicate represen- tative finite-size scan points. All curves satisfy qIread(η) = Iloc.

FIG. 3. Binder-ratio tests for the unbiased decoder along the representative line Iloc ≃0.20. (a) Measurement-probability scan at the projective limit η = 1, with predicted transition q0 = 0.20. (b)–(d) Measurement-strength scans at fixed q = 0.40, 0.60, and 0.80, with predicted transitions η0 = 0.480, 0.371, and 0.314, respectively. The vertical dashed lines mark the selected finite-size Binder crossings.

FIG. 5. Finite-size decoder diagnostics in the projective limit η = 1, with the measurement probability q varied along the horizontal axis. (a) For the biased decoder, the posterior-entropy Binder ratio locates the transition near q0 ≃0.17. (b) For the antibiased decoder, the same label-blind diagnostic gives an apparent estimate near q0 ≃0.17. (c) The label-sensitive cross-entropy variance Var(C) instead peaks near q0 ≃0.25. Vertical dashed lines mark the selected crossings or peak.
